sentences.text: Bank revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, rose from $21.0 billion in FY2016 to $28.5 billion in FY2025, a 3.5% compound rate [D5][D219].
Growth came unevenly: revenue fell 2.2% in FY2021 [D138] before rising 6.4% in FY2022 [D164] and 15.8% in FY2023 [D189].
The 15.8% FY2023 rise [D189] reflected higher rates on earning assets and the MUB acquisition [P33].
Net income rose 60.6% to $7.96 billion in FY2021 [D125][F26], driven by a provision swing to a $1.17 billion release [X141] on improving economic conditions [P57].
Payment Services was the largest contributor in FY2025, adding 1.4pp to 4.4% bank revenue growth from a 25.8% revenue share [D261][D239][D259].
Noninterest income grew 7.6% in FY2025 [D235], with payment services revenue up on merchant processing and card volumes [P11].
Consumer and Business Banking fell 3.9% and subtracted 1.3pp from growth [D252][D253], on lower net interest income from deposit mix and loan sales [P6].
Profit outgrew revenue: net income rose 20.2% [D227] against 4.4% revenue growth [D239], while noninterest expense fell 2.0% [D238].
Diluted EPS rose 21.9% [D229] against a 0.2% fall in the diluted share count [D237], so per-share growth came from earnings, not buybacks.
The efficiency ratio was 59.0% in FY2025 [D220], against a 59.3% window median [D277], a 67.4% high in FY2023 [D276] and a 55.3% low in FY2018 [D275].
That is below the 61.7% seven-bank peer median [D220][D281].
The 3.9pp fall from 62.9% in FY2024 [D195][D220] followed a 2.0% expense decline [D238], attributed to lower compensation and prior-year merger and FDIC charges [P10].
The largest window move was a 5.8pp rise to 67.4% in FY2023 from 61.6% [D144][D170], attributed to merger, MUB and FDIC special assessment costs [P30].
Credit-loss provision was 7.7% of revenue in FY2025 [D221] and fell 2.3% to $2.19 billion [X144][X145] on improved credit quality and loan sales [P12].
For a bank, operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure, so capital return against net income is the better test.
Buybacks and dividends totalled $3.66 billion in FY2025, 48.3% of $7.57 billion net income [D218][F30].
Operating cash flow was $7.97 billion, 1.05x net income [F60][D216], down 29.8% [D230], within a 0.71x to 3.63x range over FY2016 to FY2025 [D63][D140].
The pack's passages do not explain that drop, and capex is absent, so capital intensity and free cash flow cannot be assessed.
Loans were 73.5% of deposits in FY2025 [D224], and cash and equivalents of $46.9 billion fell 17.0% [F97][D232].
Return on average equity of 12.2% [D226] sat above the 11.8% seven-bank median [D283], at the 71st percentile [D282].
Buybacks rose to $489 million from $173 million [X85][X84], while dividends of $3.17 billion [X95] made up most of the $3.66 billion return [D218].
Equity rose 11.3% to $65.2 billion [D233][F114] as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D237], so book value growth came mainly from retained earnings.
Consumer and Business Banking revenue fell 10.3% in FY2024 and 3.9% in FY2025 [D249][D252], cutting its share to 31.0% from 36.6% [D251][D245].
The FY2025 segment decline is attributed to deposit mix and loan sales [P6][D252].
Credit-loss provision has run at 6.1% to 8.2% of revenue outside FY2020 and FY2021 [D43][D196], and was 7.7% in FY2025 [D221].
The 10-K reports a 66.7% efficiency ratio for FY2023 [P30], against 67.4% computed here [D170], so the 67.4% window high [D276] is not a filed figure.
Provision as a share of revenue: a fall toward the 6.1% four-bank peer median [D285] from 7.7% [D221] confirms the trend; a move above 8.2% [D196] reverses it, in the FY2026 10-K.
Efficiency ratio: staying under the 59.3% window median [D277] from 59.0% [D220] confirms the cost gains; above 61.7% [D281] reverses them, in the FY2026 10-K.
Net interest income: staying above $16.6 billion [F10] confirms the FY2025 recovery [D234]; falling below FY2024's $16.3 billion [F9] would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K.
